feature_sets.name: Local usage reconstruction
feature_sets.workflow: Select authorized source → parse provider usage → deduplicate → normalize deltas → retain history
subfeatures: metadata-only completed OpenAI API request receipts
feature_sets.decision: Implemented normalized and Claude/Codex usage imports plus metadata-only completed Claude tool pairs. Replay identities remain stable. Explicit multi-source configuration is implemented. More native tools and wider correction qualification remain planned. Completed Claude CLI result snapshots supply per-model cumulative deltas and client-side estimates without private transcript discovery. One task-owned Claude Code 2.1.308 native JSONL source now has actual first-message, resumed append, metadata projection, disjoint-token, API-revision and private dashboard proof. Repeated identical usage with different row timestamps keeps the first source event time. Changed accepted usage requires a strictly later native row and an audited ledger revision; ambiguous versions refuse. An in-memory Claude follower now reads complete appended lines incrementally, detects replacement/truncation, and keeps first accepted time for timestamp-only replay; actual owned-source idle/restart checks and fictional rotation/partial-line checks pass. A same-message later token version now atomically revises current usage with a private prior/next audit and a new ledger revision. Actual owned-source migration/replay produced no correction; changed-token behavior is qualified by fictional tests only. One historical Codex `0.162.0-alpha.17.2` JSONL source now has projected parser, cumulative-bucket, ledger replay, API and private dashboard proof. Separate per-response rows are excluded because their sum did not match final cumulative counts. An in-memory Codex follower now reads complete appended lines incrementally, with actual historical idle/restart parity and fictional append/replacement checks. Fresh Codex producer append, nonzero cache-write meaning, provider-driven segmented rotation, larger histories and general lifecycle remain unqualified. A selected historical Codex 0.162.0-alpha.17.2 file now also supplies 213 completed command/MCP/file-change tool observations with hashed IDs and no raw content; 26 outcomes remain unknown. The native follower retains exact-prefix replay and adds zero on idle replay. This is historical item evidence, not current workers, general producer-version support or billed usage. One Claude capture selection command now creates a shared-alias status/result manifest and checks existing files before publication. A prior task-owned capture replayed through selection check and terminal ingestion; it is not a fresh producer event.

feature_sets.name: Sessions, workers and live observation
feature_sets.workflow: Receive lifecycle evidence → relate sessions and children → follow in terminal or web → inspect chronology → retain stale observations
subfeatures: separate metadata-only app task observations with capture freshness
bounded app-status change inspection with explicit capture gaps
terminal app-source recovery and app-only filters
explicit CLI invocation start and terminal result
selected Codex app turn status and timing with per-task freshness
feature_sets.decision: Implemented metadata hierarchy, evidence aging, explicit multi-file health/coverage, private create/add setup checks and read-only ingestion readiness against a disposable ledger copy. Scoped chronological entity-history pages preserve process identity and one ledger revision. Shared contextual navigation is adopted without runtime authority. Native usage still supplies no live worker lifecycle; full native lifecycle adapters remain deferred. An opt-in macOS observer independently samples allowlisted AI executable basenames without arguments or environment; a bounded 60-successful-sample count/CPU/RSS trend now marks failed and missed-read gaps. Real local sampling and a private dashboard showed four matching processes, zero inferred sessions and no process/worker linkage. Optional runtime-owned normalized emission is qualified against one actual task-owned Claude review process, including running observations, heartbeats, terminal outcome and conversation-usage joining. Sessions offers scoped parent-first hierarchy and local collapse. A selected historical Codex file supplies nine paired task start/completion marker groups in a separate panel with hashed turn IDs and source-reported timing; these are not normalized session or worker lifecycle. An optional original adapter reads one selected existing CodeBurn menubar status output as replaceable recent-transcript-write evidence with source age and anonymous aliases. Its actual old, empty source proves unknown-visibility handling, not live-worker coverage. Core native provider collectors and broad discovery remain unqualified. A recent Claude/Codex OS executable sample is now compared with accepted read age for selected native inputs of the same format, explicitly without an identity link. Actual local files were historical while four OS processes were visible; no active ledger entity was inferred. One selected Claude Code 2.1.308 stdout stream is now captured as a child CLI invocation with observed start and reported end, no raw content or usage accounting. A finite real-source owner saw running then completed; the native conversation parent and OS process relation remained unknown. A separate supported app read-thread schema version 1 now supplies bounded selected Codex turn status/timing without native session-directory access. An actual finite source-to-owner-to-browser trial observed in-progress and completed turns, authoritative app-alias focus and pause-to-unknown with zero ledger activity. Per-task observation age is independent of the batch capture. This adds no usage, worker/process mapping or unattended account client. Deep selected-turn admission remains separate from its accepted app-inventory variants.

feature_sets.name: Qualified token and cost analysis
feature_sets.workflow: Filter usage → compare model/provider/surface/project/date → inspect token composition → qualify cost coverage → view explicit currency conversion
subfeatures: exact recorded session comparison at one ledger revision
download displayed aggregate report with filters and coverage
revision-pinned record-level token and cost provenance inspection
feature_sets.decision: Implemented detailed UTC period reports and qualified comparisons, project/model/day breakdowns, timed-record statistics and categorized tool activity. The browser downloads the exact displayed aggregate report with observation time, filters, revision and coverage, while the existing CLI emits the same JSON schema; neither includes raw event rows. Unsupported workflow quality remains unavailable. Richer charts and configurable views remain planned. An explicitly selected CodeBurn v74 daily cache supplies separate replaceable local-calendar aggregates, with source-reported USD of unknown billing basis and independent read/file ages. No sessions or ledger events are invented. Separate daily provider/model views preserve absent attribution and legacy unknown counters without cross-filtering marginals or summing across days. The native Codex completed-item observations now enter Report tool categories, durations and explicit error/unknown outcome counts; the same selected historical source reached the private API and dashboard. No command or result text is retained. A bounded daily tool-category chart now uses the selected normalized tool events, with explicit error/unknown counts and latest-100-date truncation. A historical authorized Codex source supplied four tool dates reconciled to 213 records; missing days do not establish agent idleness. A paged usage inspector now exposes disjoint token buckets, recorded-first cost provenance, dated per-bucket price calculations and separate missing-price/conversion states. HTTP paging pins owner/revision, CLI reads the selected ledger without initialization, and the browser supports cost filters and exact entity-history navigation. A real accepted 344-event backup supplied 131 historical usage records over three pages with all bucket totals matching independent source SQL and no missing/repeated records. Its costs remained unpriced. Pricing, conversion and recorded-zero paths are fixture-qualified, not provider-bill reconciliation. This reproduces the pinned ccusage stored-versus-calculated cost workflow using owned decimal accounting and retaining unknowns, rather than copying its floating-point/zero fallback or importing the product.

feature_sets.name: Provider quota and reset awareness
feature_sets.workflow: Use authorized supported quota source → capture named windows and reset times → show current or last-known usage with age
feature_sets.decision: Implemented normalized quota imports and opt-in installed Codex account/rateLimits/read. Native source qualified through an existing authorized login. Values retain age, reset state and unknown coverage. No hooks, login changes or credentials copied.

feature_sets.name: Pace, forecasts and budget notifications
feature_sets.workflow: Observe supported usage windows → estimate pace with explicit assumptions → compare budget → explain forecast or issue an authorized notification
feature_sets.decision: Implemented selected-window token pace and linear one-hour scenarios with observed span, sample count, heuristic confidence and partial price coverage. Opt-in on-screen UTC-day token and separate known estimated/billed cost thresholds use all accepted records, independently of filters. Claude CLI result cost is a receipt-day estimate, not individual call timing or a bill. Source, price and FX gaps remain unknown. Notifications, enforcement and quota-exhaustion forecasting remain planned. No automatic reset or paid overage.

feature_sets.name: Connected and distributed agent tracing
feature_sets.workflow: Configure authorized producer → ingest metadata spans → preserve causal hierarchy → inspect calls and failures across connected systems
feature_sets.decision: A selected OTLP/JSON trace-batch file adapter now projects completed GenAI inference tokens, agent-invocation end states and tool outcomes into the owned ledger. It removes prompt bodies and raw trace IDs and keeps cost unknown; synthetic check/preview/replay/dashboard proof only. General receivers, cloud accounts, distributed causal hierarchy and cross-format overlap reconciliation remain planned. No hooks, network receiver, credentials or upstream code copied.
